title: Intersection of two linked lists
label: idb-list
statement: Two singly linked lists may **join** at some node and share every node after it. Return the first shared node, or null if they never join — using **constant extra memory** and without changing the lists.
provenance: **InterviewDB-listed.** LeetCode 160 is on the LinkedIn list you supplied from InterviewDB. No candidate report of this exact question was found in the research passes — the evidence is that the list names it. On that list it uses the same pattern as InterviewDB Q5. Two traversals that must meet. The classic solution equalises the lengths first - the same instinct as Q5’s follow-up, where you expand the smaller frontier because the cost of a round is the size of the side you expand.

stages.title: Where they join
stages.say: Return the node where two linked lists merge, or null.
stages.require: Implement `ListIntersection.Find(headA, headB)` with O(1) extra memory. Do not change the lists. Compare nodes, not values.
testNames: same values but different nodes do not count

listen: Restates the problem and asks the clarifying questions that change the code (Compare by node identity or value? (Identity — equal values are not a ; Can the lists have cycles? (No.))
States the data structure, the invariant and the complexity before prompting
Reads AI output before running it

1.q: Why does it end when there is no join?
1.a: Both walk exactly lenA + lenB steps and become null on the same step, so `a == b` holds.

2.a: Measure both lengths, advance the longer one by the difference, then walk together.

4.a: First detect cycles (Floyd); intersection of cyclic lists is a different, harder question.

5.a: InterviewDB Q5 meets in the middle on a graph — the same "two walkers" idea.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Two singly linked lists may **join** at some node and share every node after it. Return the first shared node, or null if they never join — using **constant extra memory** and without changing the lists.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Compare by node identity or value? (Identity — equal values are not a join.)
- Can the lists have cycles? (No.)
- May I modify the lists temporarily? (No.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: If both pointers walk their own list and then switch to the other list, each walks lenA + lenB steps in total. So they reach the join at the same moment — or both reach null together, which means no join.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "T."wo pointers that each walk their own list and then the other; after lenA + lenB steps they meet at the join or both at null — O(m + n) time, O(1) memory."

learn.md:
- A HashSet of visited nodes — correct, but O(n) memory.
- Comparing values instead of references.
- Looping forever when there is no join (handled: both become null on the same step).
